solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old station broadcast repeated phrase

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of station are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: An old radio station is pumping out the same jingle over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a radio verb but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an ostinato is a short motif or rhythm persistently repeated throughout a piece.

clue.text: With two old pennies in silver cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the silver symbol wraps around the pennies and in

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money, so two of them give DD
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a couple of old pennies tucked inside silver cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' is a verb here, meaning encloses. Pre-decimal British pennies were written d.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding can work like the preposition plus or along with, as in 'adding the tip, it came to ten pounds'.

clue.text: Lawless place that may serve stew?

parts.note: read the two-word answer as instructions: its first word is an anagram signal and its second word, rearranged that way, yields the clue word stew

explanation.surface: A frontier saloon dishing out stew to cowboys.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'that may serve stew?' asks what would produce STEW, and 'wild' (a common anagram signal) applied to WEST does.
explanation.definitionFit: The American frontier of the nineteenth century is remembered as a region with little effective law enforcement.

clue.text: Sweet run for B52?

parts.note: a bombe is a frozen dome-shaped dessert, a sweet in British usage
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Asks whether a B52 is a confection, nodding to the cocktail of that name.
explanation.walkthrough: The B-52 is also a layered cocktail and a band, which makes 'Sweet' feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: The B-52 Stratofortress is a long-range US Air Force aircraft designed to drop munitions.

clue.text: James, for example, stops a person working towards same goal

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the name sits inside the word for a person like a stopper

parts.note: one can mean a person, as in 'one must be careful'
Sid James was a British comic actor of the Carry On films, so James stands for the forename Sid

explanation.surface: Someone called James blocks a teammate who is pursuing the same aim.
explanation.walkthrough: Sid James was a British comic actor from the Carry On films; 'stops' means plugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on side means being supportive and aligned with a group's aims.

clue.text: City in a word overcrowded?

parts.note: the one word overcrowded is built as over, abbreviated O as in cricket, followed by a synonym of crowded

explanation.surface: Describes a city summed up in one word as overcrowded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a word' tells you to read overcrowded as the pieces it is made of; the question mark flags the trick. O for over is a cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is the third-largest urban area in Denmark, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen.

clue.text: Am I put out to catch ball, say?

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so the word for annoyed wraps around the party

parts.note: to miff someone is to annoy or put them out
a ball is a formal dance, a do or party

explanation.surface: A cricketer wonders whether he is annoyed at being made to take a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' is a dance (DO), not a cricket ball; 'say?' tells you the definition is a fielder speaking of himself. In cricket the off side is the side the batter faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder stationed near the bowler on the off side might ask this, being that position himself.

clue.text: Weak sense about black and white's last piece

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for sense goes around the black abbreviation

parts.note: to feel is to sense

indicators.note: the last piece of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A chess player's poor sense of the board leaves white's final piece in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts FEEL around B, giving FEEBL; the last letter of 'white's' then adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble and weak are synonyms, both describing a lack of strength.

clue.text: Gunfighter can hit deck, not caught in explosion

parts.note: a billy or billycan is a tin can used for cooking over a campfire

indicators.note: an explosion blows the remaining letters apart into a new order
not means without, so the abbreviation for caught is dropped from the words hit deck

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A gunfighter can drop to the floor to avoid a blast, but not get caught in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not caught' removes one C from HIT DECK, leaving HITDEK; 'in explosion' rearranges that to THEKID.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy the Kid was a notorious outlaw and gunman of the American frontier.

clue.text: Soldier grabbing lady artist's heavenly pair

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so the soldier wraps around the artist

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: A soldier seizes a woman artist's celestial duo, perhaps a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation of the Twins, Castor and Pollux, is a pair set in the sky.

clue.text: Owing recognition certainly involves BT

indicators.note: involves means wraps up, so the word for certainly takes the two letters inside

parts.note: indeed means certainly
taken as written: BT is British Telecom

explanation.surface: A grateful nod to the phone company BT.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company, taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To be grateful to someone, owing them thanks, is to be beholden to them.

clue.text: Is back among drinkers now dry and continent

indicators.note: among means placed within the two letters for the fellowship

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a fellowship of former drinkers

indicators.note: back means reversed, so the word Is is read in the other direction

explanation.surface: Someone is back among reformed drinkers, now sober and continent in another sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continent' looks like self-restrained but is the landmass; 'back' turns IS round, and 'among' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest landmass on Earth, stretching from the Urals to the Pacific.

clue.text: Pound in Our Legend reworked Ethic of Reciprocity

indicators.note: in means the pound letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
reworked means the letters of Our Legend are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Money slipped into a reworked national legend about treating others well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' turns OUR LEGEND into GOLDENRUE; 'in' slips L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The principle of treating others as you would wish to be treated is known as reciprocity in ethics.

clue.text: Harassment in GCHQ?

definitions.meaning: persistent pestering or unwanted sexual advances
the British intelligence-gathering centre is jokingly a base for spies, who are moles

explanation.walkthrough: GCHQ is the UK government's signals intelligence headquarters; the question mark flags the punning second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Molesting someone is pestering or abusing them, so the noun means harassment.

clue.text: Topless sex toy concealed by endlessly wicked person

indicators.note: concealed by means placed inside the word for endlessly

parts.note: ever means endlessly or always

indicators.note: topless means losing the top letter, so the first letter of the toy is removed

parts.note: a dildo is a sex toy

explanation.surface: A risqué tale of a topless toy hidden by a thoroughly wicked type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' is EVER, not a deletion signal, and 'wicked person' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does evil deeds is a wicked person, a sinner or villain.

clue.text: Eastern hemisphere's quaint and charming

definitions.meaning: Europe, Asia and Africa, the lands known before the Americas, considered together

explanation.surface: Praises the eastern half of the globe as quaint and charming.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the Afro-Eurasian landmass and a picturesque antique style.

clue.text: Good move to tuck into large meatball

indicators.note: to tuck into means the pieces go inside the word for large

parts.note: fat means large
a go is a turn or move in a game

explanation.surface: A diner makes a good move and tucks into a large meatball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' looks like eating but means insertion. A faggot is a traditional British meatball of offal and herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: In British cookery this is a ball of minced pork offal and breadcrumbs, baked in gravy.

clue.text: Tees on the level in what to him should be compiling!

definitions.text: what to him should be compiling

parts.note: Tees is the setter of this puzzle, so his name stands for me
a tier is a level or layer

explanation.surface: The setter Tees, being level-headed, says compiling crosswords ought to be his calling.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by pseudonym, so 'Tees' gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's trade or vocation, the work they are suited to; for a crossword setter that is compiling.

clue.text: Ultra-conservatives in iron ships

parts.note: iron means hard, as in an iron will
liners are large passenger ships

explanation.surface: Hardened conservatives travelling in ironclad vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: People who rigidly hold to an uncompromising political position are hawks or diehards.

clue.text: Benefit within benefit gives twice the amount

indicators.note: within means the first benefit sits inside the second

parts.note: the dole is British slang for state unemployment pay
UB is the abbreviation for unemployment benefit in Britain

explanation.surface: Claiming one welfare payment on top of another doubles the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Double means twice as much, a quantity multiplied by two.

clue.text: Way to check pain in medicinal packet

indicators.note: to check means to hold back or contain, so the way wraps around the pain

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A remedy for checking pain comes in a small medicine packet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sealed sachet holds a single dose of powder or ointment.

clue.text: Heavy sea

definitions.meaning: the ocean, as in the sailor's 'the briny'

explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean intense, like a heavy sleep, and as a noun it is a poetic name for the ocean.

clue.text: Animal's revised ideas about sacrificial offering

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the animal
revised means altered, so the letters of ideas are rearranged

parts.note: a gnu is an African antelope, the wildebeest

explanation.surface: An animal's rethought ideas about a ritual offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the five letters to ASDEI, which 'about' wraps around the antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for Lamb of God, the Christian figure of sacrifice, invoked in the Mass.

clue.text: Dance in clubs with cool musician

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other two pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
in means fashionable, cool
a hop is a dance, an informal party

explanation.surface: Dancing at nightclubs with a cool musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' is the card suit, not nightspots.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish composer and pianist of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Gossip or story about King and Queen

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story wraps around the king

parts.note: a tale is a story
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Royal gossip, or a tale about a king and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip is a person who chats a lot, a chatterbox.

clue.text: Clerk is magical collaborator

definitions.meaning: a bank clerk who handles customers' cash
the silent partner of the magician Penn Jillette in the stage act Penn and ...

explanation.surface: A bank clerk turns out to be a magician's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank cashier carries this job title, and it is also the stage name of a famous silent magician.
